newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Dec 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Dec 9.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- A further step in the direction of political reform is to be taken today with the registration of candidates to write a new constitution that many hope will do away with dishonest practices. Lawyers, in their biggest political offensive, are expected to register in the highest number, hoping to form a powerful wing in the Constitution Drafting Assembly, which will comprise 76 people's representatives, one from each province, and 23 legal experts. (BANGKOK POST) (THE NATION)

- Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh wants the Air Force to move out of its hangar at Don Muang Airport to give the airport more room to expand. The Air Force would be relocated to Wing 2 in Lop Buri province and the Airports Authority of Thailand will have to pay for the move. (BANGKOK POST)

- A new beachfront property and resort adjacent to a national park in Prachuab Kiri Khan province may threaten Thailand's last habitat of some endangered birds and the park's ecological system. Forestry officials say the beach is public land which is looked after by the park and has been proposed to be included as part of the reserve, while the project's developers claim they have bought land rights papers from local villagers. (THE NATION)

- German chemical and pharmaceutical manafucturer Bayer AG will spend about 28 billion baht to build large production bases in Thailand, China and Taiwan. Thailand has been identified as the most important site in Asia, with about 12 billion baht earmarked for a regional plastics plant in the Map Ta Phut Industrial Estate, Rayong province. Bayer is seeking more land for further expansion. (BANGKOK POST)

- The Charoen Pokphand Group is considering whether to invest in a second computer chip wafer fabrication plant in Thailand or Hong Kong. The Thai conglomerate earlier announced a US$1.2 billion joint-venture with the Chinese government to construct its first plant in Shanghai, representing CP Group's entry into the upstream electronics industry. (THE NATION)

- Goodyear (Thailand) is putting pressure on Thailand to reduce import tariffs on raw materials, by using Indonesia as a bargaining ploy. The company says neighbouring countries have lower import duties on raw materials than Thailand, while Malaysia and Indonesia have no duty on raw materials for tires, including chemicals, tirecord, steel or wax oil, while Thailand still imposes various duties of between 5 to 30 percent. (BUSINESS DAY)
